subject: RFI: Dedicated inference reservation sizing — Helion AI
messages:
From: Fiona Chen <fiona.chen@helion.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, procurement@helion.ai
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Dedicated inference reservation sizing — Helion AI

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this — Helion is kicking off an RFP for dedicated inference capacity to support a mixed workload (search ranking, chat assistants, and batched embedding generation) in production Q3. We've attached our RFI template (helion_rfi_template.xlsx). Can you fill the sections below and return by end of week? A few specific asks: 

- Typical and peak throughput targets (tokens/sec and concurrent requests) per model family
- P50/P95 latency targets for 512-token and 1024-token generations
- Recommended GPU types and a reserve plan (committed vs burst lanes) with sizing rationale
- Expected reservation / lead times and earliest start date for a July contract
- Any constraints on quantization (INT8/FP16) or model kernels that would affect accuracy
- SOC 2 / audit evidence and where we can find it

Attachment: helion_rfi_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

We'd like an initial response with a filled workbook and a short pricing placeholder so our procurement and infra teams can evaluate. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min tech-scoping call.

Thanks,
Fiona Chen
Procurement Lead
Helion AI
F: +1 (415) 555-0134
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Fiona Chen <fiona.chen@helion.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated inference reservation sizing — Helion AI

Fiona — thanks for the RFI and the template. We'll take this on and return a completed workbook plus an initial sizing recommendation. I've attached our working workbook (redwood_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx) — we'll populate the Helion template fields and call out assumptions. 

Two quick clarification items that will materially change the recommended GPU mix: 
1) Model families: are you primarily running open-family LLaMA-style models (Llama2/Redwood fine-tuned derivatives) or closed decoder models (for example, GPT-3.5/4 variants)? If you have a short list of model names/versions we should assume, please paste them.
2) Latency envelope: do you require strict single-request tail latency (p95 < 200ms for 512 tokens) for all endpoints, or is it acceptable to tier latency (chat low-latency, batch embeddings higher latency)?

Assumptions we're starting with: mixed workload 60% chat (real-time), 25% embeddings (batched), 15% offline ranking (large batch). We'll propose a two-tier reserved pool (guaranteed + burst) and include an H100/A100 blend.

Attachment: redwood_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0172
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated inference reservation sizing — Helion AI (internal)

Priyom / Aditya — quick internal note to seed the workbook before we send the completed RFI. My recommended starting point based on Helion's stated workload mix: 

- GPU mix: propose 60% H100 (for 16k+ context and heavy decoder models), 40% A100 (cost-efficient for FP16 and many INT8 quantized Llama variants). Rationale: H100 provides better kernel coverage for transformer big-M models and reduces p95 for long-context workloads. A100 gives better cost curve for steady-state batched embedding throughput.
- Node count (logical sizing): target initial committed pool = 8 H100 + 6 A100 (logical), with a burst pool up to +30% for seasonality. We'll convert to physical hosts in the workbook (e.g., 1x8-H100 could map to 2x4-H100 hosts depending on instance footprint).
- Throughput targets (steady state): aim for ~20k tokens/sec aggregate (Helion app mix) steady-state, with peak burst of 35k tokens/sec during morning traffic. For embeddings: plan for 500k embeddings/hr at 768-dimension (batched).
- Latency: propose guaranteed p50 ~60ms and p95 ~180ms for 512-token generation on H100-backed routes; A100 routes optimized for throughput will have p95 ~250–300ms on 512 tokens. We'll include retry/fallback policies in the design so chat endpoints fail over to lower-cost pools gracefully.
- Quantization: recommend allowing INT8 for Llama-like families if Helion will accept a <2% quality delta; provide FP16 fallback where required. Flag: RLHF-tuned models and closed-vendor models may not be quantizable without evaluation — call this out in the RFI.

I'll populate the 'GPU mix / throughput' tab in the workbook. Aditya, please review the burst lane sizing and confirm the host packing assumptions (network egress, NVLink, and storage for model weights).

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Dedicated Solutions
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Fiona Chen <fiona.chen@helion.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Completed: Helion RFI - dedicated reservation sizing + preliminary pricing

Fiona — attaching our completed workbook and a pricing placeholder for your procurement review. Key recommendations and assumptions (summary):

- Recommended committed configuration (logical): 8 x H100 + 6 x A100 with a burst lane of +30% capacity. This maps to an initial committed pool to cover steady-state chat and embeddings, with burst for predictable morning traffic spikes.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~20,000 tokens/sec aggregate across workloads (~1.2M tokens/min). Peak burst target: ~35,000 tokens/sec. Embedding throughput planned for 500k embeddings/hr (768-dim).
- Latency expectations: p50 ~60ms, p95 ~180ms for 512-token generation on H100-backed routes. A100-backed routes prioritized for batched throughput (p95 ~250–300ms on similar workloads).
- Quantization guidance: INT8 safe for most Llama-family models with evaluation; we recommend planning for FP16 fallbacks for vendor models or RLHF-tuned checkpoints. We'll include a small accuracy verification plan in the onboarding scope.
- Timeline & lead time: earliest start date for reserved pool provisioning: July 1, 2026, assuming contract signature by June 15. Typical lead time for H100 provisioning is 3–6 weeks depending on region.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II report and audit artifacts available upon NDA; link to compliance portal included in workbook.

Attachments: helion_filled_capacity_workbook.xlsx, redwood_dedicated_pricing_helion_20260529.pdf

Next steps: 
1) Review the workbook and pricing placeholder.
2) If acceptable, schedule a 45-min technical design review to finalize host packing and model-specific kernel fit (calendar link: https://calendly.com/redwood/rdw-helion-tdr).
3) We'll run a short quantization validation with sample model checkpoints prior to provisioning.

If you'd like, we can split the proposal into a minimal committed starter + optional burst credit tranche to reduce upfront commit.

Thanks — looking forward to your feedback.

— Priyom
